skill.name: requesting-code-review
skill.description: Request and process code reviews with proper context. Use after completing significant implementation work.
skill.summary: Create structured code review requests and process reviewer feedback after significant implementation work.
skill.author: DMJGilbert

remediation.suggestion: Clarify that command examples are optional review preparation steps and should be executed only in trusted repositories.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 25 opens a Markdown bash code fence for git log and git diff examples. It is documentation, not Ruby backtick execution or dynamic shell execution.
SKILL.md line 29 is the closing Markdown fence for the prior example. It contains no executable code path or user-controlled command construction.
SKILL.md line 33 opens a plain Markdown block containing a review request prompt example. The block is instructional text, not shell or Ruby execution.
SKILL.md line 49 is a Markdown closing fence. It does not invoke commands, process input, or expose a command injection vector.
SKILL.md line 62 opens a Markdown template for review requests. The content is static documentation and does not execute external commands.
SKILL.md line 96 closes the review request template fence. It is a Markdown delimiter with no runtime behavior.
SKILL.md line 116 opens a Markdown review response example. The example is prose for handling feedback and does not execute code.
SKILL.md line 84 is a checklist item stating that unit tests pass. It contains no network scanning, host discovery, or reconnaissance instruction.
SKILL.md line 85 is a checklist item stating that integration tests pass. It does not instruct network probing or collection of external system details.

content.value_statement: Code reviews often lack context, which slows feedback and misses important risks. This skill guides structured review requests and response handling for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Defines when code reviews should be requested during development work.
Shows how to gather commit and diff context before asking for review.
Provides a reusable code review request template with testing details.
Prioritizes reviewer feedback by critical, high, medium, and low severity.
Guides responses when agreeing or disagreeing with review feedback.
limitations: Does not perform the code review itself.
Does not validate whether tests actually passed.
Requires accurate commit ranges and changed file summaries from the user.
Does not replace project-specific review policies or compliance checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature Review
use_cases.description: Create a clear review request after finishing a major feature branch.

use_cases.title: Review Subagent Work
use_cases.description: Request review after each task in a multi-agent implementation workflow.

use_cases.title: Handle Reviewer Feedback
use_cases.description: Sort feedback by severity and prepare concise responses for fixed or deferred items.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after completing a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Request a code review for my latest changes. Include the changed files, the purpose of the work, and tests I ran.

prompt_templates.title: Feature Branch Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before merging a completed feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a review request for commits [base]..[head]. Summarize the feature, key files, requirements, tests, and areas needing attention.

prompt_templates.title: Subagent Task Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a subagent finishes one implementation task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a reviewer prompt for the task just completed. Include the task goal, commit range, changed files, risks, and verification performed.

prompt_templates.title: Review Response Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after receiving detailed review comments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize this review feedback by severity. Mark what must be fixed now, what can be deferred, and where I need a technical response.

output_examples.input: I finished a bug fix and need review before merging.
output_examples.output: A structured review request with commit range, branch, summary, changed files, test checklist, concerns, and reviewer questions.

output_examples.input: The reviewer left critical, high, and minor comments.
output_examples.output: A prioritized response plan that separates blocking fixes, current-session fixes, documented deferrals, and justified disagreements.

output_examples.input: A subagent completed one task in a larger implementation plan.
output_examples.output: A focused review prompt that explains the task outcome, files changed, requirements, and areas requiring extra attention.

best_practices: Include the exact commit range and branch in every review request.
List tests performed and clearly mark any tests not completed.
Respond to disagreements with technical evidence and specific trade-offs.
anti_patterns: Requesting review without explaining the requirements or changed files.
Treating low severity feedback as more urgent than blocking issues.
Dismissing reviewer concerns without evidence or a clear response.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after significant implementation work, before merging, after complex bug fixes, or during subagent-driven workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill review code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare review requests and process feedback, but a reviewer still evaluates the code.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the commit range, branch, changed files, requirements, tests performed, and any areas needing extra attention.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when preparing AI-assisted review prompts.

faq.question: How does it handle critical feedback?
faq.answer: Critical feedback should be fixed immediately and should block other work until resolved.

faq.question: What if I disagree with a reviewer?
faq.answer: Provide technical evidence, explain trade-offs, reference relevant code or documentation, and remain open to correction.
